feature: About The 99 — the reference page, its gate and its figures
note: One route, and the close-out's job is the page a reader actually gets rather than the route existing. Three rows, because the page has reader STATES that no single shot shows. A reader at version 0 sees every entry and nothing marked; a reader who is behind sees the eyebrow, the marks and the dismiss; a reader who is current arrives from the account menu and has no dismiss to press, because there is nothing to acknowledge. The version the reader has acknowledged lives in `user_prefs`, so those states are reached by URL rather than by data edits where possible — `?next=` is what the gate appends, and the dismiss prints and carries it. The account menu row is deliberately NOT here. It is the page's permanent entry point and the one surface outside `/about` this feature changed, but every verb in this script reaches page content through `onPage`, which scopes to `<main>` — and the shell's account trigger sits outside it by construction. A row for it could only be written by defeating that scope, which is the rule that stopped two probes measuring the shell while naming a page. It is covered instead by `account-menu.test.tsx`, which asserts the row's position, its link, the roving wrap past it and its busy state, and by the close-out walk. No `shares` block: every figure mounts an app component in ONE place, so there is no second route to be the same as — the sameness question this feature has is whether a figure matches the surface it documents, which is what `figures.tsx` asserts per figure and what this sheet shows in a glance.
